layer_description: siliceous hardpan below unconsolidated loamy sand; top of hardpan at approximately 1 m
spatial_scope: AU-ASM tower (soil moisture sensors above and within the hardpan)
method: soil moisture sensors installed at ~1 m above and within hardpan
citation: Eamus D, Huete A, Cleverly J, Nolan RH, Ma X, Tarin T, Santini NS (2016) Mulga, a major tropical dry open forest of Australia: recent insights to carbon and water fluxes. Environ. Res. Lett. 11:125011
quote: One moisture sensor was located at approximately 1 m depth in unconsolidated soil; a second sensor was located at the same depth but within the hardpan.
note: Hardpan top varies laterally around 1 m (one sensor at ~1 m is above it, the other at the same depth is inside it). Hardpan water content 0.05 m3/m3 with only minor fluctuations since 2010; soil above it 0.08-0.35. Same page: 'Mulga trees have a small but significant proliferation of roots near the top of the hardpan' and a perched water table forms above it after big rains. Figure redrawn from Cleverly et al. 2016b (Sci. Total Environ. 568:1227-1237; ScienceDirect blocked, not read). Hardpan thickness not given.

layer_description: shallow siliceous hardpan (Ti Tree basin)
spatial_scope: Ti Tree basin soils generally; Mulga at AU-ASM tower is one of the study sites
citation: Rumman R, Cleverly J, Nolan RH, Tarin T, Eamus D (2018) Speculations on the application of foliar 13C discrimination to reveal groundwater dependency of vegetation and provide estimates of root depth and rates of groundwater use. Hydrol. Earth Syst. Sci. 22:4875-4889
locator: Sect. 1 Introduction; Sect. 2.1 Site description; Sect. 4 Discussion
quote: A. aneura is shallow-rooted and associated with shallow hard pans in this catchment (ca. 1 m below ground surface; Cleverly et al., 2016a, b)
note: Sect. 2.1: hardpan is 'a common formation in the top 1-1.5 m in this type of soil'; Discussion: 'shallow (< 1.5 m) hardpan'. Depth statements cite Cleverly et al. 2016a,b. AU-ASM is at the spot-sampling site with depth to groundwater 49.5 m.

layer_description: Mulga (Acacia aneura) root system above the hardpan
citation: Eamus D et al. (2016) Environ. Res. Lett. 11:125011
locator: p. 11, Sect. on ecohydrological niche separation
quote: Mulga is shallow rooted (<2 m), evergreen and located above a shallow hard pan (Cleverly et al 2016b).
note: Original: Cleverly J et al. (2016b) Soil moisture controls on phenology and productivity in a semi-arid critical zone. Sci. Total Environ. 568:1227-1237 (doi:10.1016/j.scitotenv.2016.05.142; not accessible). <2 m is an upper bound; roots concentrate at the hardpan top (~1 m).

layer_description: regional water table well below the hardpan
citation: Eamus D et al. (2016) Environ. Res. Lett. 11:125011
quote: The siliceous hardpan is buried below the surface and prevents drainage of water to the regional water table, which is 49 m deep at this site (Cleverly et al 2016c).
note: Original: Cleverly et al. 2016c Agric. For. Meteorol. 220:151-159 (not read). Rumman et al. 2018 give 49.5 m in the text and 49.4 m in the Fig. 1 caption for the AU-ASM tower. Groundwater is out of reach of roots.

layer_description: deepest TDR probe pair
citation: OzFlux. Alice Springs Mulga - Measurements (web page)
quote: Soil moisture - TDR Campbell CS610 ... -1.0m to -1.2m
note: Quote rebuilt from table cells (cells split in the page). Deepest probe sits at about the hardpan top.

layer_description: large rock (core stone or boulder) at 1.5 m occupying half of the soil pit
spatial_scope: Daintree Rainforest Cow Bay core 1 ha plot; data-file coordinates -16.23819 145.42715 are identical to the AU-Cow tower coordinates
method: soil pit 1.5 m deep, 0.6 m wide, 1.2 m long; probes installed
citation: TERN. Daintree Rainforest, Cow Bay Soil Characteristic Data 2011-2014 (dataset metadata, Lineage)
quote: at 1.5 m depth a big rock was discovered which occupied half of the pit
note: Rock occupied only half the pit, and a deeper pit beside it reached 2.0 m in soil (see D02), so it is a stone or boulder, not continuous bedrock. Parent rock not named.

layer_description: soil sampled and probed at 2.0 m (no bedrock reached)
spatial_scope: Cow Bay core 1 ha plot (tower coordinates)
method: soil pit; lab analysis at 0.15, 0.75, 1.5 and 2.0 m
citation: TERN. Daintree Rainforest, Cow Bay Soil Characteristic Data 2011-2014 (metadata and Cow_Bay_soil_characteristics_data_1.1.csv)
locator: Lineage section; data file rows soilDepth_metres 0.15-2
quote: A smaller, deep pit was dug inside the main pit avoiding the rock and going down to 2.0 m
note: Minimum soil depth 2.0 m (bottom of pit, not of soil). Lab clay at 2.0 m = 36.8 % (CSV). The 0.75 m row has clay_percentage 224.19, an obvious data error. CS616 volumetric water content at 2.0 m was about 0.27 on 1 Jan 2013 (pit data CSV), so water is stored at that depth.

layer_description: deepest soil water content probe
citation: OzFlux. Cow Bay - Measurements (web page)

citation: OzFlux. Calperum - Measurements (web page)

note: Tower soil pit (2012, Landscape Science group) described to 140 cm with bulk density to 145 cm, all in calcareous fine sand without rock (rows AU-Cpr-E02 to E07 of literature_soil_evidence_20261103.csv; not re-read here). A search-engine excerpt of the landscapescience.org Calperum page (server refused connection, so unverified) says the calcareous fine sandy clay 'continues beyond 2.5 metres depth' and the regional aquifer is 'at least 35 metres below the land surface'.

layer_description: soil water monitored over at least the top 2.5 m
spatial_scope: Calperum Mallee SuperSite (tower is part of it)
method: SuperSite soil water content monitoring (depths not listed)

quote: the top 2.5m of soil has essentially been dry since the end of 2017
note: Shows that soil (not rock) extends to at least 2.5 m and that water use reaches this depth. Same page: researchers aim to quantify water 'from the deeper subsoil, and potentially from the regional groundwater'. Mallee root depth not found.

layer_description: soil moisture profile from surface to 2.5 m
method: volumetric soil moisture profile (sensor type not given)

quote: volumetric soil moisture (θv, m3 m-3) from surface to 2.5 m depths were measured at both sites
note: The OzFlux measurements page lists only CS616 at -0.05 and 0.50 m (see D02). Same paper Sect. 2.1: soils are red Kandosols 'characterised as deep, sandy loams' and the UC site is representative of savanna 'found on deep, well drained sandy loam soils'. No bedrock or laterite depth given.

layer_description: OzFlux-listed soil moisture probes

quote: Soil moisture (two replicates) | Campbell Scientific | CS616 | -0.05, 0.50m
note: Probably the standard flux-file probes; the 2.5 m profile in Bristow et al. 2016 is additional.

layer_description: A horizon 0.20 m + B horizon 0.69 m (atlas values)
spatial_scope: Digital Atlas of Australian Soils / ASRIS mapping unit at the site
citation: Whitley R, Beringer J, Hutley LB, et al. (2016) A model inter-comparison study to examine limiting factors in modelling Australian tropical savannas. Biogeosciences 13:3245-3265
locator: Table 1, Daly Uncleared column, A and B horizon Thickness (m)
quote: Thickness (m) 0.20 ... Thickness (m) 0.69
note: Sum of atlas A+B thickness = 0.89 m; this is described solum depth, not depth to rock. Footnote: 'Soil descriptions are taken from the Digital Atlas of Australian Soils'. Every soil field in the Daly Uncleared column equals the Sturt Plains column except Type (likely copied). Conflicts with 'deep, sandy loams' and the 2.5 m moisture profile.

layer_description: model: 0.6 m to 'bedrock' layer is one class; total soil block 30 m freely draining
spatial_scope: VOM model set-up for all NATT sites (AU-How, AU-DaS, AU-Dry, AU-Stp, Adelaide River)
citation: Nijzink RC, Beringer J, Hutley LB, Schymanski SJ (2022) Does maximization of net carbon profit enable the prediction of vegetation behaviour in savanna sites along a precipitation gradient? Hydrol. Earth Syst. Sci. 26:525-550
locator: Sect. 2.2.1, p. 528; Supplement S8 soil tables ('0.60-bedrock')
quote: This was achieved by a total soil thickness of 30 m and a fast drainage parameterization
note: The '60 cm-bedrock' class in Supplement S8 is a model layer running from 0.6 m to the 30 m model base, not a measured bedrock depth. Sect. 4.2: a borehole about 2 km from Daly River 'suggested deeper groundwater tables' (Supplement Fig. S2.8, graph only; no number read). Model rooting depth range 1.0-9.0 m for perennial plants (S8).

layer_description: OzFlux-listed soil moisture probes
citation: OzFlux. Dry River - Measurements (web page)

note: No deeper profile found for Dry River.

spatial_scope: Digital Atlas of Australian Soils / ASRIS mapping unit at the site
citation: Whitley R et al. (2016) Biogeosciences 13:3245-3265
locator: Table 1, Dry River column, A and B horizon Thickness (m)
quote: Thickness (m) 0.15 ... Thickness (m) 1.29
note: Atlas solum depth, not depth to rock. Same table gives clay A horizon over clay B (red Kandosol) from the atlas.

layer_description: model: 0.6 m to 'bedrock' class; total soil block 30 m
spatial_scope: VOM model set-up for NATT sites
citation: Nijzink RC et al. (2022) Hydrol. Earth Syst. Sci. 26:525-550
locator: Sect. 2.2.1; Sect. 4.2; Supplement S8 and Fig. S2.11
quote: This was achieved by a total soil thickness of 30 m and a fast drainage parameterization
note: '60 cm-bedrock' is a model layer, not a measurement. One borehole about 13 km from Dry River 'suggested deeper groundwater tables' (graph only).

layer_description: gridded GSDE soil depth attribute
spatial_scope: global 1 km GSDE grid (Shangguan et al. 2014) as compiled by Shi et al. 2025
citation: Shi J et al. (2025) A flux tower site attribute dataset intended for land surface modeling. Earth Syst. Sci. Data 17:117-134; dataset doi:10.5281/zenodo.12596218
locator: netCDF variable Soil_depth (unit cm), attribute source
quote: Soil_depth = 10 ; Soil_depth:source = "Shangguan et al., 2014, https://doi.org/10.1002/2013MS000293"
note: NOT site evidence; listed only so it is not mistaken for one. The same dataset gives Soil_depth = 100 cm (also GSDE) for AU-DaS, AU-Stp, AU-Cpr and AU-How. The 10 cm conflicts with the atlas 1.44 m and the 0.5 m probe.

layer_description: unconfined water table in Bassendean sand (Gnangara system)
citation: Moore CE, Thompson SE, Beringer J, Cooper W, Gelsinari S, Nguyen HL, Wang H, Xie Q, Silberstein RP (2025) Biophysical response of a coastal woodland to extreme water deficit during a year of record-breaking heat. Environ. Res. Lett. 20:034043
quote: The groundwater depth at Gingin has dropped from 9.6 m below land surface when the flux tower was establishment to nearly 11.0 m in 2024
note: 'establishment' sic. Sect. 3: depth to water exceeded 10.8 m by end of the 2023 water year; Sect. 4: more than 10.5 m. Abstract: about 4 m decline since 1977. value_m_best 10.5 is the recent-years level quoted in Sect. 4. Sect. 4 says the water table is near 'the maximum root extent known for banksia woodland species (Groom 2004)' and that Jan-Apr 2024 ET was probably all groundwater, so roots reach the water table.

layer_description: water table (older value)
citation: OzFlux. Gingin - Site Description (web page)
quote: The watertable is at about 8.5 m below the surface
note: Older figure, superseded by D01. Same page: 'fine sediments, sometimes diatomaceous, hold water and they have perched watertables each winter'.

layer_description: vadose-zone EnviroScan profile to 9.05 m
method: Sentek EnviroScan capacitance profile at 16 depths
citation: Moore CE et al. (2025) Environ. Res. Lett. 20:034043
note: Unsaturated zone storage '~3.3 m, with porosity of 0.3'. OzFlux measurements page also lists a neutron probe 'Every 25cm from the surface to 12m, 3 holes', CS616 to 1.6 m and piezometers at -15 m.

layer_description: Bassendean sand, E2 horizon 103 to 500+ cm; auger could not go deeper
spatial_scope: Bassendean reference profile about 5 km ESE of AU-Gin tower (Gnangara-Moore River State Forest)
method: pit to ~2 m plus sand auger
citation: Turner BL, Laliberte E (2020) Proposal for a new Bassendean reference soil in Western Australia. J. R. Soc. West. Aust. 103
quote: we could not retrieve samples deeper than 5 m due to the incoherent nature of the sand
note: Sand continues below 5 m (bottom open). Same profile: 'Roots were present throughout the profile to at least 300 cm.' Tower soils have discontinuous coffee-rock (Podosol) layers (Moore et al. 2025 Sect. 2.1), which this profile lacks.

layer_description: deep-rooted Banksia trees tapping groundwater
citation: Groom PK (2004) Rooting depth and plant water relations explain species distribution patterns within a sandplain landscape. Funct. Plant Biol. 31:423-428
quote: access groundwater up to a maximum depth of 9 m depth during the summer months
note: Abstract attributes this to earlier work on deep-rooted Banksia trees (original not named in the abstract). With the water table now 10.5-11 m (D01), the tower stand is at or beyond this limit, as Moore et al. 2025 note.

layer_description: tree roots through duricrust to the dry-season water table
citation: Hutley LB, O'Grady AP, Eamus D (2001) Monsoonal influences on evapotranspiration of savanna vegetation of northern Australia. Oecologia 126:434-443 (UTS author manuscript)
quote: Roots reached depths of approximately 10 m, the depth of the water table at the end of the dry season (Cook et al. 1998).
note: Preceding sentences: excavation at Howard Springs showed root biomass mostly in the top 1 m of sandy loam, but 'large diameter roots (> 3 cm) of mature trees were able to extend through weaknesses in the duricrust and access water stored in the heavier clay sediments of the sub-soil'. Trees extract water from the sub-soil (> 3 m).

layer_description: water table at end of dry season
citation: Hutley LB, O'Grady AP, Eamus D (2001) Oecologia 126:434-443 (UTS author manuscript)
quote: Roots reached depths of approximately 10 m, the depth of the water table at the end of the dry season (Cook et al. 1998).
note: Original: Cook PG et al. (1998) Water balance of a tropical woodland ecosystem, Northern Australia. J. Hydrol. 210:161-177 (ScienceDirect blocked; AGRIS abstract has no depth). Wet-season level not given.

layer_description: main root system in top 4-5 m; single roots to 9 m
citation: Schymanski SJ, Sivapalan M, Roderick ML, Beringer J, Hutley LB (2008) An optimality-based model of the coupled soil moisture and root dynamics. Hydrol. Earth Syst. Sci. 12:913-932
quote: The root system of the vegetation on the site is mainly limited to the top 4–5 m of soil (Kelley, 2002), with single roots observed at depths of up to 9 m
note: Original: Kelley G (2002) PhD thesis, NTU/CDU (download blocked). Model used a constant 5 m rooting depth. Chen et al. 2003 (Oecologia 137:405, UTS manuscript p. 26) repeat 'up to 5 m (Kelley et al. 2002)' and roots observed to 9 m (A. O'Grady pers. comm.).

layer_description: weathered laterite (C horizon) / ferricrete duricrust of low permeability over clay sub-soil
spatial_scope: Howard Springs (Schymanski) and three NATT sites generically (Hutley 2001)
citation: Schymanski SJ et al. (2008) Hydrol. Earth Syst. Sci. 12:913-932; Hutley LB et al. (2001) Oecologia 126:434-443
quote: weathered laterite in the C horizon, below about 1.2 m (Kelley, 2002)
note: Hutley 2001: clay sub-soils 'at depths greater than 1-1.5 m'; 'ferricrete boulders can occur in a matrix of mottled, heavy clays forming a duricrust of low permeability and variable depth'. Chen et al. 2003 (Darwin region): 'Prominent macropores, often containing tree roots, are found in this layer.' Not a root barrier: roots pass to ~10 m (D01, D03).

layer_description: late Tertiary sediment mantle over bedrock
spatial_scope: lowland plains around the site (sediment mantle); 15 m = model pedosphere depth
citation: Schymanski SJ et al. (2008) Hydrol. Earth Syst. Sci. 12:913-932
quote: a late Tertiary depositional surface, with a sediment mantle that seldom reaches more than 30 to 40 m in depth
note: Same section: 'we interpreted the catchment as having an average depth of the pedosphere (Z) of 15 m'. 15 m is a modelling choice, 30-40 m the stated upper bound of the sediment mantle.

layer_description: 77-90 % of root biomass in upper 0.5 m; trenches to 2 m
spatial_scope: Eucalypt open forest near Darwin; Chen et al. 2003 say the trenches were at the Humpty Doo study site
method: trench excavation to 2 m around 16 trees
citation: Eamus D, Chen X, Kelley G, Hutley LB (2002) Root biomass and root fractal analyses of an open Eucalyptus forest in a savanna of north Australia. Aust. J. Bot. 50:31-41
quote: About 77-90% of total root biomass was found in the upper 0.5 m of soil.
note: Biomass distribution only; excavation stopped at 2 m, so it says nothing about maximum depth.

layer_description: OzFlux-listed soil moisture probes
citation: OzFlux. Howard Springs - Measurements (web page)
quote: Soil moisture | Campbell Scientific | CS616 | 10-100cm
note: A search-engine excerpt (not verified) says Hutley et al. 2000 Funct. Ecol. used capacitance soil water to 3 m depth (Wiley blocked).

layer_description: OzFlux-listed soil moisture probes
citation: OzFlux. Sturt Plains - Measurements (web page)
quote: Soil moisture (two replicates) | Campbell Scientific | CS616 | -0.05, -0.50m
note: No soil-depth, calcrete or rock statement found for Sturt Plains.

layer_description: A 0.20 m + B 0.69 m (atlas values; column looks copied from Daly Uncleared)
spatial_scope: Digital Atlas of Australian Soils mapping unit

quote: Thickness (m) 0.20 ... Thickness (m) 0.69
note: Every soil field except Type is identical to the Daly Uncleared column, so this is weak evidence. Grey Vertosol (cracking clay).

note: '60 cm-bedrock' is a model layer. Two boreholes about 10 km from Sturt Plains 'suggested deeper groundwater tables' (graph only).

layer_description: profile described to 2.42 m; C horizon 1.62-2.42 m medium sandy clay loam with 2-10 % granodiorite fragments; no rock reached
spatial_scope: CEOP Tumbarumba station (coordinates -35.65043 148.15125, about 0.7 km N of OzFlux coordinates)
citation: CEOP Murray-Darling Basin Reference Site: Tumbarumba station page (NCAR/EOL CEOP archive)
quote: C 1.62 - 2.42 m Yellowish brown (10YR5/4-Moist)
note: C horizon contains '2-10%, Granodiorite, coarse fragments' (weathering granodiorite). Bedrock depth not stated. A search-engine excerpt of the COSMOS probe 077 page (server refused connection, unverified) says 'red dermosol, 3 - 4 m deep'. OzFlux measurements page returned 404; site page says only that TDR is used, no depths. The f09 grid value 0.91 m is not supported.

layer_description: deepest soil moisture probe
citation: FFPRI FluxNet. 安比森林気象試験地 (Appi) site page
note: Translation: 'buried depths 5, 15, 30, 50, 80 cm'. Soil temperature 2-80 cm. Soil: Andosol, moderately moist brown forest soil BD(d). No soil-depth or bedrock statement on the page.

layer_description: most plant roots in upper 25 cm
citation: Koarashi J et al. (2025) Radiocarbon-derived ages of carbon in live, dead, and newly emerged fine roots in a cool-temperate Japanese beech forest. Front. For. Glob. Change 8
quote: Plant roots are mostly present in the upper 25 cm of the soil
note: Original: Nakanishi et al. 2012 (not read). Bulk root distribution, not a maximum. Soil cores in that study were only 20-25 cm long.

layer_description: deepest soil moisture sensor; soil temperature sensors to 1 m
method: soil moisture at 0, 0.1, 0.2 m; soil temperature 0-1 m
citation: NIES CGER GEM. 富士北麓サイト (Fuji Hokuroku site) page
quote: 土質：富士山の粗粒火山灰土
note: Quote translation: 'Soil: coarse-grained volcanic ash soil of Mt Fuji'. Depths from the same table: soil moisture 0 (3 sites), 0.1 (2), 0.2 (2); soil temperature down to 1. A 1 m soil-temperature sensor suggests diggable material to 1 m (my inference). No lava, scoria-thickness or root data found; JP-Fjy (bare lava) is about 1.2 km away (my calculation from coordinates).

layer_description: almost no soil layer: litter and its decomposition products on exposed Kenmarubi lava
citation: FFPRI FluxNet. 富士吉田森林気象試験地 (Fujiyoshida) site page
locator: Site outline; 土壌タイプ field
quote: 溶岩流の上に位置するため土壌の発達はきわめて悪く，落葉落枝とその分解物を除き土層はほとんど見られません．
note: Translation: 'Because the site lies on a lava flow, soil development is extremely poor, and apart from litter and its decomposition products almost no soil layer is seen.' Soil type: '未熟土、lm (剣丸尾溶岩流上、溶岩が露出)' = immature soil, on Kenmarubi lava flow, lava exposed. value 0.0 = mineral soil thickness, not an observed number. Roots must use lava fissures; no data on that. CLM will raise anything to 0.4 m.

layer_description: soil temperature thermocouples only; no soil moisture measured
citation: FFPRI FluxNet. 富士吉田森林気象試験地 (Fujiyoshida) site page
note: Translation: 'buried depths 0.02-0.5 m' (soil temperature). The page lists no soil moisture or groundwater observation. Sensors to 0.5 m show some buriable material (litter, scoria or lava rubble) at the instrument spot (my inference).

layer_description: soil moisture probes
citation: FFPRI FluxNet. 鹿北流域試験地 (Kahoku) site page
quote: 土壌水分（含水率） Campbell, CS616-L 埋設深 0.05, 0.10 m
note: Translation: 'soil water content, Campbell CS616-L, buried at 0.05 and 0.10 m'. Soil temperature to 0.50 m. Soil: moderately moist brown forest soil BD; geology crystal schist (FWDB, No.3 sub-watershed). No soil depth found.

layer_description: penetrometer-measured surface soil (Nc 0-5) and weathered layer (Nc 5-40) thickness; schist basin has thicker weathered layer on lower slopes
spatial_scope: Kahoku No.3 sub-watershed (crystal schist); the tower is in the adjacent No.2 sub-watershed
citation: Onuki Y, Yoshinaga S, Araki M, Ito E, Shichi K, Shimizu A (2003) 森林流域の土層厚分布様式の推定 (Estimating soil-layer thickness distribution in forested watersheds). 114th Annual Meeting of the Japanese Forest Society, abstract
note: The abstract gives no numbers for Kahoku (quote left empty for that reason); full text not available. Shows that Kahoku soil and weathered-layer thickness were measured; the numbers would be in the FFPRI watershed reports.

layer_description: deepest tensiometer; TDR at 0.1 m; groundwater-level gauge at 1.4 m
method: tensiometers 0.05-0.90 m; CS-650 TDR 0.1 m; pressure water-level gauge 1.4 m
citation: FFPRI FluxNet. 札幌森林気象試験地 (Sapporo) site page
locator: Observation items: 土壌水分; 地下水位
note: Translation: 'buried depths 0.05-0.90 m' (tensiometers). The groundwater-level gauge (Druck PDCR940) is buried at 1.4 m, which suggests a water table that is at times shallower than 1.4 m (my inference; no water-table values read). Soil: moderately moist black soil BlD (volcanic ash, Andosol per Yamanoi et al. 2015). No soil depth found.

layer_description: soil moisture probes
method: soil moisture at 0.15 and 0.4 m; soil temperature 0.01-0.5 m
citation: AsiaFlux. TKY site information page
quote: Soil moisture measurement depths: 0.15 and 0.4 m
note: Quote is the page's table content as returned by the page reader, not a sentence. Soil type listed as Brown forest soil (Dystric Cambisol), though other sources say Kuroboku (Andosol).

layer_description: soil organic matter inventory to 1 m depth (>300 tC/ha)
citation: Ohtsuka T (2012) Carbon cycling at Takayama Forest (review). Jpn. J. Ecol. 62:31-44
quote: SOM 1 m 300 tC ha-1 Jia
note: Japanese characters could not be extracted from the PDF; the quote keeps only the Latin characters of the sentence (SOM pool exceeds 300 tC/ha to 1 m depth, Jia and Akiyama 2005). Original: Jia S, Akiyama T (2005) Agric. For. Meteorol. 134:70-80 (not read). Implies soil at least 1 m deep at the stand.

layer_description: O ~0.10 m (mor), A ~0.20 m, B ~0.30 m; bedrock Cretaceous sedimentary rock
spatial_scope: CC-LaG tower area (13.7 ha clear-cut, flat terrace)
citation: Takagi K, Takahashi Y (2022) Site information sheet, Micrometeorological CO2 Flux Data at Teshio CC-LaG Experiment site (TSE), NIES
quote: The bedrock was Cretaceous sedimentary rock. The dominant soil was a Gleyic Cambisol (FAO 1988) with about 10 cm of O horizon, with a mor humus type, 20 cm of A horizon, and 30 cm of B horizon
note: 0.5 m = A+B mineral thickness, 0.6 m including O. The sheet does not say the B horizon sits directly on rock, and no C horizon is described. Soil temperature sensors go to 1.2 m (D02), so material below the B horizon can be dug. Gleyic = seasonally wet.

layer_description: deepest soil moisture probe; soil temperature to 1.2 m
method: CS615 at -5, -10, -30, -60 cm (1 profile) and -5, -10 cm (4 profiles); Pt thermometers to -120 cm
citation: Takagi K, Takahashi Y (2022) Site information sheet TSE, NIES
note: Soil temperature: -1, -5, -10, -20, -40, -80, -120 cm (one profile).

layer_description: volcanic-ash loam (Kanto Loam) about 2 m thick over Joso clay
citation: Suh S, Lee E, Lee J (2009) Temperature and moisture sensitivities of CO2 efflux from lowland and alpine meadow soils. J. Plant Ecol. 2:225-231
quote: Volcanic ash soil forms a loam layer of 2 m in the study area, as is found widely distributed over central Japan.
note: The Joso clay below is also unconsolidated, so 2 m is not a rock contact. Regional stratigraphy (CEOP Tsukuba page): loam 1.5-2.0 m, Joso clay 2.5-9 m, sand 9-30 m.

layer_description: water table generally within the Kanto Loam or the Joso clay
spatial_scope: Tsukuba area (regional, CEOP Tsukuba reference site)
method: stratigraphic description citing Tosaki et al. (2008)
citation: CEOP Tsukuba Reference Site. Land cover page (University of Tsukuba)
quote: The water table is generally observed within the Kanto loam or the Joso clay.
note: No number given. Layer depths on the page: 'a loam layer (1.5-20. m; the Kanto Loam), a clay layer (2.5-9 m; the Joso clay)' ('20.' probably a typo for 2.0). TERC runs observation wells 2.2, 10 and 22 m deep (Ioka et al. 2004, TERC Bull. 5:99-101; Japanese text could not be extracted, so no water-table values read).

layer_description: A horizon (surface organic-rich layer) about 0.10 m over volcanogenous regosol (Tarumae tephra)
spatial_scope: pre-2004 TMK larch plantation tower, same plantation, about 0.5 km from the JP-Tmd tower
citation: Hirano T, Hirata R, Fujinuma Y, et al. (2003) CO2 and water vapor exchange of a larch forest in northern Japan. Tellus B 55:244-257
quote: The soil was a volcanogenous regosol with high water permeability and poor nutrients. The thickness of the surface organic layer (A horizon) was about 10 cm.
note: No pumice or root data in this paper. Unverified search-engine summaries (Takahashi et al. 2008 JGR, Wiley blocked; Sano et al. 2010 / Yazaki et al. 2016, Elsevier/MDPI blocked) say roots are scarce below 20 cm and the A horizon lies over a pumiceous layer. Nearby FRED profiles in Tomakomai Experimental Forest show roots to 0.31-0.55 m in Tarumae pumice (JP-Tom-D01, D02).

layer_description: TDR soil water probes
method: TDR (CS615) at 5 and 10 cm; soil temperature 5-50 cm
citation: Hirano T et al. (2003) Tellus B 55:244-257
quote: Soil water content was measured at 5 and 10 cm at three points with TDR sensors (CS615, CSI, USA).
note: The NIES TMK site information sheet (SiIn_TMK_2001-2003_05.pdf) lists the same TDR depths. No information found for the post-2012 JP-Tmd tower.

layer_description: small roots in buried 2C pumice gravel layer 30-55+ cm (bottom of profile)
spatial_scope: Tomakomai Exp. Forest compartment 129, Horonai basin, deciduous broadleaf secondary forest (same forest type as JP-Tom); distance to tower not known
citation: Hokkaido Univ. FSC FRED Soil Database, profile TK01 (source: Shibata H. 1996, PhD thesis, Hokkaido University)
locator: Profile table, horizon 2C, 根系 column
quote: 30～55+ | 2C | ... | れき層 | 15mmの軽石富む | ... | 小根含む
note: Translation: '30-55+ cm, 2C, gravel layer, 15 mm pumice abundant, small roots present'. Roots also in C1/C2 pumice (10-25 cm) and abundant in buried 2AC (25-30 cm). So Tarumae pumice here is permeable to roots; maximum root depth is below the 55 cm profile bottom.

layer_description: no roots in buried 2C pumice gravel 31-72+ cm
spatial_scope: Tomakomai Exp. Forest compartment 115, Pinus strobus plantation (not the JP-Tom stand)
citation: Hokkaido Univ. FSC FRED Soil Database, profile TK02 (Shibata 1996 thesis)
locator: Profile table, horizon 2C, 根系 column
quote: 31～72+ | 2C | ... | れき層 | 35mm以下の軽石富む | ... | 根無し
note: Translation: '31-72+ cm, 2C, gravel layer, pumice up to 35 mm abundant, no roots'. Small roots present to 31 cm (A, C1, C2, 2AC). Conifer plantation, so the root limit may be stand-specific.

layer_description: extremely thin topsoil on Tarumae volcanic ash, very well drained
citation: Tomakomai Experimental Forest web site (立地・気候 page)
locator: 立地・気候 (site and climate) text
quote: 研究林の全域は樽前山由来の火山灰土壌で覆われており、水はけが非常によく、きわめて薄い表土が5～10cm堆積します。
note: Translation: 'The whole forest is covered by volcanic-ash soil from Mt Tarumae; drainage is very good and an extremely thin topsoil of 5-10 cm has accumulated.' Topsoil only: pumice below holds roots and water (D01). Same page: soil freezes to about 30 cm in the forest.

layer_description: soil temperature sensors to 1 m; soil moisture depths not listed
citation: AsiaFlux. TOE site information page
note: These are soil temperature depths; no soil moisture depths are given. Soil type: Volcanogenous regosol.

layer_description: deepest TDR soil moisture probe; groundwater not observed
citation: FFPRI FluxNet. 山城水文試験地 (Yamashiro) site page
locator: Observation items: 土壌水分; 地下水位
note: Groundwater level: '観測無し' (not observed). Soil type: immature soil Im, on weathered granite.

layer_description: poorly developed soil in sandy weathered granite with thin O and A layers
spatial_scope: Yamashiro 1.7 ha watershed with the flux tower
citation: Jomura M, Kominami Y, Tamai K, Miyama T, Goto Y, Dannoura M, Kanazawa Y (2007) The carbon budget of coarse woody debris in a temperate broad-leaved secondary forest in Japan. Tellus B 59:211-
quote: The forest soil is poorly developed in sandy weathered granite with thin O and A layers.
note: No number. The often-cited 'average depth 47 cm' (Forests 2022, 13:510) could not be read (MDPI 403) and was seen only in a search-engine excerpt. Weathered granite below the soil is likely partly usable by roots and water, but no Yamashiro measurement was found.

layer_description: thin, immature, sandy soil over weathering granite
citation: Miyama T, Kominami Y, Tamai K, Goto Y, Kawahara T, Jomura M, Dannoura M (2006) Components and seasonal variation of night-time total ecosystem respiration in a Japanese broad-leaved secondary forest. Tellus B 58:550-559
quote: The valley is underlain by weathering granites, and the soil layer is generally thin, immature, and sandy.
note: Agrees with Jomura et al. 2007 (D02). Still no measured soil thickness read; the 47 cm figure remains unverified.
